notes.note: Welcome to Firefox Enterprise. Version 158 is our first public release. Firefox Enterprise is built for organizations with strict security, governance, and compliance requirements. It combines the familiar Firefox browser with additional security controls and an admin console that organizations can run on their own infrastructure. IT teams can use the console to centrally configure browser policies, manage access to web applications, control how sensitive data is shared, and govern the use of AI tools.

**Company sign-in:** Employees sign in with your organization's single sign-on before the browser opens. Firefox Enterprise works with any identity provider that supports OpenID Connect (OIDC), including the multi-factor authentication your provider requires.

**Device posture checks:** Firefox Enterprise reports the security posture of each device to your admin console, including the operating system, disk encryption, whether endpoint security software is running, whether the device is joined to an Active Directory domain, installed extensions, and network details. Admins can require a specific posture before an employee can sign in, and Firefox Enterprise signs the employee out if their device stops meeting it. If security logging is turned on, blocked sign-ins and posture-based sign-outs are recorded in your admin console.

**Data loss prevention:** Admins can warn about or block pasting, file uploads, downloads and printing on the websites they choose, with a message they write explaining why. All checks run in the browser on the device, so content is never sent over the network to be inspected. If your organization already uses a third-party DLP agent that connects to Firefox through Content Analysis, Firefox Enterprise turns off built-in DLP and defers to your agent. DLP are recorded in your admin console, and admins can turn this off if they don't require it.

**Watermarking:** Admins can stamp a watermark across sensitive pages, such as the employee's email address and the time. This discourages leaks, and if a screenshot is shared, it can be traced back to the session it came from. Admins choose the text, color and the websites it appears on.

**Lockdown mode:** Admins can apply extra security restrictions to specific websites, giving organizations a way to protect sensitive web apps without a virtual desktop (VDI) or remote browser isolation (RBI). On a protected site, Firefox can turn off JavaScript just-in-time compilation, block service workers, load the site over HTTPS only, and open it in its own container. Containers can also be temporary, so the site's data is cleared when its last tab closes. Employees see an icon in the address bar when such protections apply.

**Profile data encryption:** Bookmarks, history, form data, cookies, and cached web content are now encrypted on disk by default, using a key provided by your admin console. This helps protect the data if the profile folder is copied from a device without access to the encryption key.

**Access Connector:** Employees can access internal company sites and web apps from personal devices without a device-level VPN, supporting bring-your-own-device (BYOD) use. Admins specify the address of a proxy running on their organization’s infrastructure through the console. An icon in the address bar indicates when a site uses the connector. If the connector can’t be reached, Firefox shows an error.

**Policies via Admin Console:** Firefox Enterprise applies policies set by admins via the Admin Console, and many policy-driven changes take effect without restarting the browser. Admins can also make the console the only source of policies, ignoring any set locally on the device.

**Sign-out, session lock rules**: Admins choose whether employees are signed out when Firefox Enterprise closes, restarts or crashes. When the browser isn't set to sign out on close, the session is locked instead, and employees unlock it with their operating system's sign-in, such as Touch ID on macOS or Windows Hello, rather than going through company single sign-on again.
**Update control:** Admins choose which Firefox Enterprise releases their devices run and when they update, and can make the browser restart automatically once an update is ready to install.

**Security event logging:** Admins can turn on logging for security events, including downloads, printing, extension installs, visits to websites blocked by policy, and unsafe websites and downloads flagged by Safe Browsing. Each type of event is off until an admin turns it on, and admins choose how much detail to include: full web addresses, just the domain or none, and for downloads, full file details or just the file type. Events go to your organization's admin console, not to Mozilla.
When employees sign in, Firefox Enterprise shows a company badge with a notice that the browser is managed by their organization and some activity may be monitored.

Firefox Enterprise omits some features that don't apply at work. New Tab doesn't show sponsored stories or sponsored shortcuts, and Firefox VPN, Firefox Relay email masks, breach alerts and extension recommendations aren't included. When Sync is turned off by policy, Firefox Enterprise doesn't prompt employees to sign in to Sync or show tabs from other devices.
Firefox Enterprise profiles can only be opened by Firefox Enterprise, not by regular Firefox.
Firefox Enterprise has its own branding on the splash screen and New Tab.

You can find information about policy updates in the [Firefox 158 release notes for admins][1].

  [1]: https://firefox-admin-docs.mozilla.org/release-notes/version/firefox-158/

system_requirements:
## Windows

### Operating Systems (32-bit and 64-bit)
 - Windows 10 or later

### Recommended Hardware
-  1 gigahertz (GHz) or faster compatible processor or System on a Chip (SoC)
-  1GB of RAM / 2GB of RAM for the 64-bit version
-  500MB of hard drive space

---

## Mac

### Operating Systems
- macOS 10.15 or later 

### Recommended Hardware
- Macintosh computer with an Intel x86 or Apple silicon processor
- 512 MB of RAM
- 200 MB hard drive space

---

## GNU/Linux

### Software Requirements

*Please note that GNU/Linux distributors may provide packages for your distribution which have different requirements.*

- Firefox will not run at all without the following libraries or packages:
    - glibc 2.17 or higher (glibc 2.28 or higher on arm64)
    - GTK+ 3.14 or higher
    - libglib 2.42 or higher
    - libstdc++ 4.8.1 or higher (libstdc++ 6.0 or higher on arm64)
    - X.Org 1.0 or higher (1.7 or higher is recommended)
- For optimal functionality, we recommend the following libraries or packages:
    - DBus 1.0 or higher
    - NetworkManager 0.7 or higher
    - PulseAudio
text:
Firefox Enterprise 158 builds on Firefox 158, including its security fixes and web platform improvements. See the [Firefox 158 release notes][1] for details.

  [1]: https://www.firefox.com/en-US/firefox/158.0/releasenotes/
